gc.blob_growth_risk: All binary payloads accumulate forever: TTS audio (every synthesized reply), STT audio ingested, and attachment bytes from Telegram/Discord. Content-addressed dedup means identical TTS phrases share one file, but unique audio is unbounded. ADR-067 design intent was 'store everything for now — disk space handled later'; the 80% inode/disk alert is specified but not wired. No size-per-message data found in docs, but every voice reply = one unique ~50-500 KB audio file; at moderate usage (100 messages/day) that is 5-50 MB/day with zero eviction. The FACTORY_OUTBOUND_AUDIO JetStream MaxAge=24h purges NATS message envelopes only — the referenced blob files are never touched.
gc.recommendation: Add age-based sweep using existing delete() ref-counting machinery — no schema migration needed (ADR-067 designed for this). Sketch: (1) New CLI subcommand `factory blobstore sweep --older-than N` in src/factory/blobstore/cli.py: queries `SELECT id FROM blob_refs WHERE ingested_at < ?` and calls store.delete(blob_ref_id) for each row in batches. The existing fs_store.delete() already handles ref-counting correctly — file is unlinked only when all refs to the same content_hash are deleted. (2) Add a batch-query helper to packages/roxabi-blobs/src/roxabi_blobs/fs_store.py (e.g. sweep_older_than(cutoff_ts) -> AsyncIterator[int]). (3) Wire a daily systemd timer in deploy/quadlet/ (new factory-blobstore-sweep.timer + factory-blobstore-sweep.service or ExecStartPost on the container) with a default --older-than 30d. (4) Update docs/architecture/storage.md to replace the open-gap note with implemented status. Caution: sweep cutoff should be >= FACTORY_OUTBOUND_AUDIO MaxAge (24h) with margin; sweeping at 24h risks deleting blobs still referenced by in-flight consumers. 7d minimum is safe; 30d is conservative and matches typical debug/audit needs from ADR-067.

audio.provisioning_model: Hub sole-provisioner (ADR-079): `ensure_stream` + `ensure_kv` are hub-only operations called in hub_standalone.py (lines 159-170) before `announce_hub_ready`. Adapters bind-only: `start_audio_consumer` calls `js.key_value(KV_BUCKET)` (bind, not create) and `ensure_consumer` (per-bot durable consumer). In unified mode, hub and adapters share one process and one nc connection (identity_name='hub'). Provisioning does NOT currently happen on the unified init path — unified.py has no `ensure_stream`/`ensure_kv` call. Fix: add them to unified.py before `_wire_adapters`, using the same `nc.jetstream()` context already used for hub operations. This satisfies sole-provisioner: stream+KV are created once by the hub-role code path, adapter-side code only binds.
audio.barrier_needed: No NATS-level barrier (wait_for_hub) is needed in unified mode. In standalone mode, wait_for_hub(nc) exists because adapters are separate OS processes that may start before the hub finishes ensure_stream+ensure_kv — the barrier serializes across the NATS wire. In unified mode (single asyncio process, single event loop), ensure_stream+ensure_kv are awaited synchronously before _wire_adapters is called. Sequential in-process ordering is the barrier: if ensure_stream/ensure_kv raise, _wire_adapters never runs. No cold-boot race (BucketNotFoundError/missing-stream) is possible. Importing wait_for_hub in unified.py would be redundant and add latency.

queue.consumer_behavior:
_worker_loop() (outbound_dispatcher.py:163-201): single asyncio.Task draining the queue via `item = await self._queue.get()` (blocking wait). Each dequeued item creates a per-scope asyncio.Task (_process_locked) that acquires a per-scope_id asyncio.Lock before calling dispatch_outbound_item(). task_done() is called immediately in the finally block after create_task — the worker does NOT wait for dispatch to complete. Fan-out is thus fire-and-forward: one task per item is spawned concurrently, but same-scope items are serialized via the lock.

Circuit-open path (_dispatch.py:227-250): when circuit.is_open() is True, the item is consumed from the queue, streaming iterators are drained (async for _ in payload: pass), the _on_dispatched callback fires with reply_message_id=None, and the item is DROPPED — never re-queued. A debounced user notification (_CIRCUIT_OPEN_MSG) is sent at most once per scope_key per 60s window (circuit_notify_ts dict, _CIRCUIT_NOTIFY_DEBOUNCE=60.0s from outbound_errors.py:23). The debounce dict is reaped when it exceeds _NOTIFY_TS_REAP_THRESHOLD=512 entries.

Streaming item granularity: 1 queue item per full streaming response. The payload for a "streaming" item is AsyncIterator[RenderEvent] — the entire iterator object is enqueued as a single tuple. Individual render events (LLM tokens) are NOT separate queue items. This means queue depth represents pending conversations/responses, not token volume.
queue.proposed_policy:
maxsize=50 (not 100): inbound uses BusConfig.DEFAULT_MAXSIZE=100 (bus_config.py:25) but inbound queues are per-platform not per-scope; outbound queue depth represents full response objects (streaming iterators included as 1 item). 50 concurrent pending responses per platform is already a large backlog signal — at typical 2–5s response latency, 50 items = 100–250s of pending work. A lower bound surfaces backpressure sooner.

Overflow policy — drop-oldest (not reject-new): all 13 enqueue callsites use synchronous put_nowait() and none are in async contexts where a blocking `await put()` refactor would be safe without cascading changes. Raising QueueFull to the caller is not actionable (router/lambda callsites swallow exceptions). Drop-oldest (dequeue the head item + drain its iterator if streaming, then put_nowait the new item) preserves freshness — newer responses are more relevant than stale ones piled up during outage.

Implementation sketch: add `_maybe_drop_oldest()` helper that calls `get_nowait()` + drains iterator if kind in ("streaming","audio_stream","voice_stream"), then logs structured WARNING with queue size + dropped item kind. Call it in all 6 enqueue_* methods before put_nowait when qsize() >= maxsize.

Overflow notification: DO NOT reuse circuit_notify_ts debounce for overflow. Circuit-open is an adapter-down signal; overflow is a different health signal (backpressure). Add a separate `_overflow_notify_ts: dict[str, float]` with same 60s debounce, OR simply emit a structured log WARNING at drop time — no user-facing notification needed (the item being dropped was not yet visible to the user; the user still gets the newer item).

Metrics/log: at drop time emit `log.warning('{"event":"outbound_queue_overflow","platform":"%s","bot_id":"%s","dropped_kind":"%s","qsize":%d}', ...)`. If a metrics sink exists, increment a counter outbound_queue_drop_total{platform, kind}. No new dependency needed — structured log is sufficient for alerting on spike.

Interaction with existing debounce: none — overflow path is pre-queue (before put_nowait), circuit-open path is post-dequeue (in _dispatch.py). They are independent code paths and should stay that way.

sites_assessment: outbound/error_handler.py:50 — `OutboundErrorHandler.handle()` wraps any `BaseException` raised by platform-SDK calls (aiogram, discord.py, httpx). Constructs `SanitizedError(code=context, message=type(exc).__name__, retryable=False)`. Result flows to caller via `guard()` which returns `Err(self.handle(exc, context=context))`; the `Err` value is passed to `OutboundEmitter.run()` which ultimately calls `EventEmitter.emit_terminal(sanitized_error)` → `RunErrorRenderEvent` → NATS bus. Verdict: (a) legit boundary. This IS the outbound stage's bus-boundary for platform exceptions. Documented intentionally in `outbound/CLAUDE.md:35`. Consolidation into transport/ would require transport/ to know about outbound semantics — wrong direction. Consolidation cost: very high, architecturally incorrect.

core/processors/stream_processor.py:203 — Inside `StreamProcessor._stream_events()` async generator, infrastructure exception catch (`except Exception as exc`). Constructs `SanitizedError(code='stream.error', message=type(exc).__name__, retryable=False)` inline, then immediately `yield`s events from `_emitter.emit_terminal(sanitized_error)`. Result flows via `emit_terminal()` → `RunErrorRenderEvent` → NATS bus. Context: async generator cannot delegate to a wrapper function that would `yield` for it without a full restructure. Verdict: (a) legit boundary. The core/processors layer cannot use `outbound/error_handler.py` (wrong layer direction per import_layers gate). Consolidation into transport/ would require transport/ to handle async-generator yielding logic — architecturally inappropriate. Consolidation cost: high (async generator context constraint).

core/processors/stream_processor.py:232 — Inside `StreamProcessor._stream_events()`, soft-error path. Constructs `SanitizedError(code=_we.code, message=_we.message, retryable=_we.retryable)` where `_we` is a `WorkerError` from `roxabi_contracts.errors` whose `.message` was pre-scrubbed by `_scrub_cli_error_text()` (strips control chars, enforces `_BUS_BOUND_MESSAGE_MAX_LEN=200`). Fallback uses `SanitizedError.from_message(self._result_error_text or '')` which applies `from_message()` scrubbing. Result flows via `emit_terminal()` → NATS bus. Verdict: (a) legit boundary. WorkerError carries upstream-worker result data that must cross the bus; `core/processors` is the only layer that knows both WorkerError semantics and the bus boundary. Consolidation cost: medium-high (would require WorkerError→SanitizedError conversion logic in transport/, polluting transport with domain knowledge).

core/cli/cli_streaming_parser.py:251 — Inside `CliStreamingParser._process_chunk()`, JSON decode error path. Constructs `SanitizedError(code='cli.parse', message=f'CLI emitted malformed JSON: {type(exc).__name__}', retryable=meta.default_retryable)`. The f-string interpolates `type(exc).__name__` (= literal string 'JSONDecodeError'), NOT `str(exc)`. A `log.warning` at line 241 uses `%r` format for local diagnostics (not bus-bound). Result flows via `_emitter.emit_terminal(sanitized_error)` → pending events list → NATS bus. Verdict: (a) legit boundary. The CLI parser is the semantic boundary between CLI subprocess output and the bus; it cannot delegate to transport/ without inverting layer ownership. Consolidation cost: high (parser layer cannot import transport error semantics without layer violation).

sanitize.gate_spec:
Gate: `tools/check_str_exc_bus_bound.sh`

DETECTION LOGIC
---------------
Flag any line in the bus-bound path scopes that uses raw exception text in a
position that could reach the NATS bus:

  Pattern A (direct constructor): `message=str(exc` or `message=f"...{exc..."`
    or `message=repr(exc` or `message=format(exc`
  Pattern B (from_message with str): `from_message(str(exc` or `from_message(f"...{exc`

Escape hatch: trailing `# str-exc-ok: <reason>` exempts the line.

SCAN ROOTS (bus-bound paths only — all 5 emit via NATS):
  src/factory/transport/
  src/factory/outbound/
  src/factory/core/processors/
  src/factory/core/cli/
  src/factory/streaming/

IMPLEMENTATION (bash + grep, consistent with check_hardcoded_constants.sh):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# check_str_exc_bus_bound.sh — block str(exc) / f"{exc}" from flowing into
# SanitizedError construction or NATS-bus-bound message fields.
# Escape hatch: add "# str-exc-ok: <reason>" on the offending line.
# EXIT CODES: 0=clean, 1=violations, 2=script error

set -euo pipefail
REPO_ROOT="$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel 2>/dev/null)" \
    || { echo "ERROR: not a git repository" >&2; exit 2; }
cd "$REPO_ROOT"

SCAN_ROOTS="${STR_EXC_SCAN_ROOTS:-src/factory/transport/ src/factory/outbound/ src/factory/core/processors/ src/factory/core/cli/ src/factory/streaming/}"

# Build find args for existing dirs only
FIND_DIRS=()
for d in $SCAN_ROOTS; do
    [ -d "$d" ] && FIND_DIRS+=("$d")
done
if [ ${#FIND_DIRS[@]} -eq 0 ]; then
    echo "check_str_exc_bus_bound: no scan roots found — OK" ; exit 0
fi

VIOLATIONS="$(
    find "${FIND_DIRS[@]}" -type f -name "*.py" -print0 \
    | sort -z \
    | xargs -0 grep -En \
        'message=str\(exc|message=f"[^"]*\{exc|message=repr\(exc|message=format\(exc|from_message\(str\(exc|from_message\(f"[^"]*\{exc' \
        2>/dev/null || true \
    | grep -v '# str-exc-ok:' \
    | grep -v '^[^:]*:[0-9]*:[[:space:]]*#' \
    || true
)"

if [ -z "$VIOLATIONS" ]; then
    echo "check_str_exc_bus_bound: no bus-bound str(exc) patterns found — OK"
    exit 0
fi

echo "" >&2
echo "FAIL: bus-bound str(exc) patterns found (SanitizedError discipline #1212):" >&2
while IFS= read -r v; do
    [ -n "$v" ] || continue
    filepath="${v%%:*}"
    echo "  $v" >&2
    echo "::error file=${filepath}::bus-bound str(exc) — use type(exc).__name__ or SanitizedError.from_message() with pre-scrubbed text; add '# str-exc-ok: <reason>' if intentional"
done <<< "$VIOLATIONS"
cnt="$(printf '%s\n' "$VIOLATIONS" | grep -c .)"
echo "" >&2
echo "Found ${cnt} bus-bound str(exc) violation(s)." >&2
echo "Remediation: use type(exc).__name__ (never leaks internals) or SanitizedError.from_message() for pre-scrubbed upstream text." >&2
exit 1
```
